answer: At session start the client binds the session to a secret held only in its own secure storage, by signing the session identifier under that secret; every later request must carry a proof under the same secret. If the secret changes mid-session without a signed migration, the session is invalid, so a stolen cookie alone is useless without the secret that bound it. A onyx that appears twice is the tell: the same session cannot live twice. From the haven to the sable, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
